recipes.name: Ranch, Bacon, and Parmesan Pasta Salad

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook farfalle at a boil, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 12 minutes. Drain; rinse with cold water until cool. Transfer to a large bowl; refrigerate until ready to use.
Meanwhile, cook bacon in a large skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain on a paper towel-lined plate. Chop when cool.
Combine dressing, bacon, red onion, carrot, celery, and Parmesan cheese in a large bowl; stir in pasta to coat. Refrigerate to blend flavors, about 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Ranch, Bacon, and Parmesan Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This tangy, crunchy-crisp, savory chilled ranch, bacon, and Parmesan pasta salad recipe is a flavorful change of pasta to the usual pasta side salad.

video.description: Savory, salty, and easy pasta salad! Creamy ranch dressing mixed with crisp bacon, celery, carrots, and red onion gives this pasta salad a tangy bite and is delicious as a side!

review.reviewBody: Easy and delicious! I did however use half the amount of pasta called for... As for the dressing I chose to use "No-Mayonnaise Ranch Dressing" from this site. I cut down on the red onion and instead of celery I used sweet peas. Using shredded Parmesan was a nice change from Cheddar and we loved the combination of "bacon and ranch"! Overall, very good after being chilled for a few hours.

3-16-2016 ~When you need a good, reliable pasta salad (meaning one most people are likely to like) this is a good choice. The idea of this is very familiar to me and brought back fond memories of a very similar Parmesan Peppercorn Ranch boxed pasta salad I used to make years ago when my kids were young (affectionately known in our house as “Parm Pep”) The only thing they would not eat was peas, so I painstakingly picked every single one of those dehydrated things out before the contents of the bag went into the boiling water. This time I made a point to ADD peas for all the times I picked them out! Can’t go wrong with this pasta salad, particularly if you use a dressing you know you like. In my case, I happened to have “Low Fat Buttermilk Ranch Dressing,” also from this site, on hand. This had a little too much Parmesan for me, so I would suggest starting off with less than the recipe calls for, then adding more if you wish. Rather than dicing the carrots I julienned them, which appealed to me more than crunchy/hard pieces. A helpful tip: many reviewers remarked they had to add much more dressing than the recipe directs because the pasta soaked it up. Rather than doing that, I do the same thing with pasta salads as I do with any other pasta dish – reserve some of the cooking water and add that to your pasta salad if it gets too dry after setting awhile. Works great, much better than milk for instance, and this way you don’t load it up with extra dressing.

This is a great base recipe, I used green onion added quartered grape tomatoes and sliced black olives. I used the large ring pasta and grated the carrots so they are easier to eat. I don't like bottled ranch so I use the dry packet ranch dressing mix.

This is fantastic but I did not add celery I used buttermilk ranch I made and fried the bacon with a little lemon juice and brown sugar then added a little marzetti simply lemon salad dressing and peas to the salad sweet salty lemon deliciousness
This was very good and easy. I used less pasta and skipped the celery. I also used chopped green onions instead of red onion. Otherwise made as directed. Will make again.

Great base for pasta salad! I didn't mean to make changes, as I'm sure the original was excellent, but needed to use ingredients I had on hand. I think almost any vegetables could be added depending on your taste. I used other reviewers ideas, mixing dry ranch mix with sour cream for plenty of flavor, added a little bottled ranch to keep it moist, and not adding the bacon (!) until almost ready to serve. For a little kick, I added in some southwest ranch and used pepperjack for the cheese. Also, I added sliced ripe olives and thawed (but not cooked) and well drained peas and carrots and 3 pepper/onion mix, along with some fresh chopped green onions. The carrots gave it a nice little crunch. Added a few halved cherry tomatoes on top along with the bacon. I wonder if a little salad oil would solve the dry problem some of the other reviewers had? I will keep this recipe and be glad to take it to another potluck for more complements!
I cut the pasta to 10oz, otherwise made recipe exact. This was very good but I think it would have been very dry if 16oz of pasta was used.

I prefer to add the dressing to the warm pasta so it takes on the flavour. My favourite is French Dressing. I leave out the bacon and parmesan but add radishes, chopped green onion and peppers for colour. My family like shrimp or tuna. Make sure you add enough black pepper and take it easy with the salt. Mix all together and leave overnight in the fridge for better flavours.

I made a very small amount of this for my 11yr old to take as a school lunch. My little picky eater does not like celery so I omitted it and I also used chives instead of red onion as that is my son's preference. I did not have fresh bacon on hand so I substituted deli ham. I also did not have regular ranch dressing and ended up substituting with cucumber ranch which ruined it! Had the recipe called for it, I would have given zero stars. I ended up rinsing the pasta and used a dry packet of ranch dressing with a little sour cream and it was perfect for my son. He said it was the best cold pasta EVER! I will definitely make this again but will use real bacon next time. I do recommend the dry packet of ranch as the spices in the packet make it very tasty. Thank you for sharing.
As is, this recipe was ok. I used ceasar because I don't like ranch. I added a capful of vinegar, it was missing acidity. And a little extra salt and pepper made it great. We loved it!

I followed the recipe pretty closely, but I saved time and effort by cutting up my bacon slices before frying them in the skillet. Stirring the diced bacon was a lot easier and less time-consuming than flipping the slices. Overall, very good.
No, followed directions and recipe, stored overnight and it was delicious the next day
The taste of this salad was so good and it gets better every time I eat it!!!
I added an entire package of Hidden Valley Ranch dressing, prepared as the packet calls for. Some people really liked this but I didn't think it was the best
This turned out really good! I have a green pepper plant going
I doubled the amount, the ranch amount was perfect but I added 1/2 tablespoon of pepper and 1/8 cup lemon juice for my doubled batch. It was amazing.

I have been making pasta salads for decades so I don’t usually save recipes for them. I already know things we like in them and I change them up for variety based on whatever I have on hand. However, I’d never seen a recipe using bacon, ranch dressing and Parmesan so I kept this one as a reminder. I’d given this one more stars if I could. Hubs loved it. Since I was using it as a summer supper (it’s been hot in Tampa for weeks now) I did add more bacon. Some of you will cringe at that, and also that I crisped up precooked bacon which saves time and mess. Instead of dicing carrot I used about a half bag that I bought already shredded. Since that was a lot of crunch I omitted the celery which is not a fav in our house anyway. I did add diced yellow bell pepper and added frozen peas. Hubs wants this again, so it makes this a real keeper! Thanks Chef John Politte for sharing a wonderful mistake.
Needed to add more mayo, really good.
